title: Borrow timeline
subtitle: Each bar is a borrow, alive from creation to its last use. Hover a bar to see its lines.

scenarios.label: Many readers
scenarios.text: Two shared borrows overlap freely. Both end at their last use on line 4, so v.push on line 5 can take an exclusive borrow. Under the old lexical rules they would have lived until the end of the block (dashed) and this would not compile.

scenarios.label: Read, then write
scenarios.text: first points into the vector's buffer. push may reallocate that buffer, which would leave first dangling. Because first is used again on line 4, the shared borrow is still alive when the exclusive one starts.

scenarios.label: Two writers
scenarios.text: Two exclusive borrows of the same value overlap on lines 3–4. Even single-threaded, two live &mut would break the guarantee that whoever holds &mut sees no surprise changes.

scenarios.label: NLL in action
scenarios.text: r1 is last used on line 3, so its borrow ends there, not at the closing brace. The shared borrow r2 starts afterwards: no overlap, no error. This is what non-lexical lifetimes (Rust 2018+) bought us.

errors: error[E0502]: cannot borrow `v` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable
error[E0499]: cannot borrow `s` as mutable more than once at a time
